questions.text: What coefficient word format and scaling should the filter use?
questions.default: Q1.15 signed 16-bit coefficients, output is accumulator >>> 15
questions.reason: Keeps coefficients and output in 16 bits with full scale near 1.0, and the request does not give a format.
questions.answer: Q1.15 signed 16-bit coefficients, output is accumulator >>> 15

questions.text: How should the accumulator be rounded before it is cut to 16 bits?
questions.default: Truncate (arithmetic shift, no rounding bias added)
questions.reason: Truncation needs no extra adder and is the simplest bit-exact model for the reference model.
questions.answer: Truncate (arithmetic shift, no rounding bias added)

questions.text: What happens on overflow beyond the 16-bit output range?
questions.reason: Saturation avoids wrap-around spikes in a low-pass output and is cheap in logic.

questions.text: What are the coefficient values after CPU reset?
questions.default: All 32 coefficients zero, so RESULT is zero until the host loads them
questions.reason: The request does not give a filter response, and zero is a known safe state that the host overwrites.
questions.answer: All 32 coefficients zero, so RESULT is zero until the host loads them

questions.text: What UART baud rate and framing should the test shell use?
questions.default: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (BAUD_DIVIDER 868)
questions.reason: 115200 8N1 is the usual USB-UART setting and 868 cycles at 100 MHz gives under 0.2 percent error.
questions.answer: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (BAUD_DIVIDER 868)

questions.text: How does the host frame register writes and reads over UART?
questions.default: Write: byte 'W' (0x57), 1 byte offset, 4 bytes big-endian data. Read: byte 'R' (0x52), 1 byte offset, device returns 4 bytes big-endian
questions.reason: The request does not give the shell framing, and a fixed-length frame is simple to test.
questions.answer: Write: byte 'W' (0x57), 1 byte offset, 4 bytes big-endian data. Read: byte 'R' (0x52), 1 byte offset, device returns 4 bytes big-endian

questions.text: What happens when SAMPLE_IN is written while a run is in progress?
questions.default: The write is ignored and STATUS bit 0 stays set
questions.reason: A single MAC cannot take a second sample mid-run, and ignoring keeps the delay line consistent.
questions.answer: The write is ignored and STATUS bit 0 stays set

questions.text: When do coefficient writes take effect during a run?
questions.default: Coefficient writes are accepted at any time and apply from the next filter run
questions.reason: Avoids mixing old and new coefficients inside one output sample.
questions.answer: Coefficient writes are accepted at any time and apply from the next filter run

questions.text: Is the reset button active low and should it be synchronised?
questions.default: CPU RESET (C12) is active low and passes through a two-flop synchroniser before use
questions.reason: The Nexys A7 CPU reset is active low and asynchronous to clk, so synchronising avoids metastability.
questions.answer: CPU RESET (C12) is active low and passes through a two-flop synchroniser before use
